evidence.description: REQ-124's own Edge Cases (lines 229-236) and Acceptance Criteria (238-244) describe the cross-loan tx_hash collision purely in terms of an identical-string tx_hash -- they never once consider that the SAME real transaction's hash can reach loanRows.tx_hash via one code path (facilitator-returned, lending-orchestrator.mjs:423) and reach a fresh reconcile candidate via a structurally DIFFERENT code path (RPC-log-extracted, lending-verify.mjs:174), with no code-level guarantee the two serialize identically. REQ-124 as specified is therefore not sufficient to guarantee the money-safety property its own Root Cause paragraph claims to close.

Both new FIND-201 tests (cross-loan-replay-rejected and genuinely-new-tx-positive-control) use the IDENTICAL literal string for the stored loanRows.tx_hash and the mock log's transactionHash -- no fixture exercises a case-differing pair representing the realistic facilitator-format-vs-RPC-format source mismatch this finding identifies. lending-orchestrator.test.mjs:375-407's own wiring-assertion test (receivedLoanRows) likewise never exercises casing.

Both alreadyCredited (verifyRepayment) and alreadyRecorded (reconcileProvisionalDisbursement) use raw `row.tx_hash === txHash` -- case-sensitive strict equality, no normalization -- while this SAME codebase's own lending-signer.mjs:32-34 addressesEqual() explicitly lowercases both sides of the structurally-identical hex-string-identity problem for wallet addresses (REQ-119). The inconsistency is a genuine implementation gap, not a stylistic nit, given tx_hash values are sourced cross-process (escrow.mjs:133 facilitator JSON vs. lending-verify.mjs:174 own-RPC eth_getLogs, see FIND-301 for the full trace).

goNoGo: NO-GO, unconditionally, for certifying this iteration as the final gate for ONGOING lending. Exactly as in iteration-3: TODAY's specific, narrow, one-time transition (loan_Franklin_1 -> disbursement_failed-or-refused, with no tx_hash yet recorded to collide against) is independently re-verified safe by direct code trace. What this review blocks is broader: FIND-301 shows that REQ-124's own cross-loan tx_hash-replay guard -- the fix this feature's iteration-3 review explicitly declined to wave through without -- itself silently depends on an unverified, untested, and (given the facilitator is an external x402-rs submodule not present in this checkout) unverifiable-from-this-repo assumption: that a transaction hash string returned by the facilitator's own HTTP JSON API and the SAME transaction hash string returned by this codebase's own eth_getLogs RPC call share identical character casing. This codebase already knows, and already handles, this exact class of problem for wallet addresses (lending-signer.mjs's addressesEqual) but has not applied the same discipline to tx_hash. Recommend: normalize tx_hash to lowercase at every storage and comparison site (mirroring addressesEqual's own established pattern) before this feature is certified for the colony's ongoing, repeated lending operation; add a test fixture proving the guard survives a casing mismatch between the two source formats. Not required before a single, manually-supervised recovery of loan_Franklin_1 itself (which has no tx_hash yet to collide against) -- required before this protocol is trusted to run repeated cold-start cycles unattended.
